title: Multiomic profiling of responses to clinical and novel bisphosphonates reveals extraskeletal effects on ageing related signatures.
authors: Lu, Jinsen; Rao, Srinivasa Rao; Knowles, Helen; Zhan, Haoqun; Gamez, Beatriz; Qin, Mingyu; Platt, Eleanor; Frost, Lucy R; Allen, Tiffany-Jayne; Marshall, Gayle; Huber, Kilian V M; Bauer, Ludwig G; Vendrell, Iolanda; O'Brien, Darragh P; Kessler, Benedikt; Horne, Anne; Reid, Ian R; Bountra, Chas; Kirkland, James L; Khosla, Sundeep; Ebetino, Frank H; Roldan, Emilio; Russell, R Graham G; Edwards, James R
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用多组学与AlphaFold靶点解析探讨双膦酸盐的抗衰老作用，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Bisphosphonates (BPs) have been used effectively to treat excessive bone loss for over 50 years. Recent clinical evidence suggests extra-skeletal benefits but how this occurs remains unknown. Here we use a panel of human, murine and cellular assessments to chart BP-induced ageing-related changes both systemically and at local organ sites. In vivo spatial transcriptomics in aged mice treated with zoledronate showed a shift in cellular composition towards that of young animals specifically in heart, liver and intestine, with upregulation of genes governing detoxification, mitochondrial stability, energy metabolism, and antioxidation. A 5000-plex randomized trial based human proteomic analysis showed significant alterations in ~400 proteins after zoledronate treatment, with downregulation of proteins linked to genomic instability, proteostasis loss, mitochondrial dysfunction, stem cell exhaustion, and SASPs. Fluorescent labeling and tracing confirmed uptake of bisphosphonates by non-skeletal cells. In addition, low doses of several common, clinically utilized BPs stimulated growth and protected against DNA damage-induced senescence in multiple human cell types, with strongest effects in cardiomyocytes. Finally, proteome-wide target deconvolution with AlphaFold identified previously unrecognized binding partners, including PHB2 and ASAH1, and downstream upregulation of MEF2A was validated to be a key mediator of zoledronate triggered benefits in cardiomyocytes. Collectively, these results identify potential geroprotective mechanisms for BP action in multiple non-skeletal tissues.
abstract_zh: 双膦酸盐（BPs）已被有效用于治疗过度骨丢失超过50年。近期临床证据提示其具有骨骼外益处，但具体机制尚不明确。在此，我们利用一组人类、小鼠及细胞层面的评估，系统性地描绘了BP诱导的与衰老相关的变化，涵盖全身及局部器官位点。对经唑来膦酸治疗的老年小鼠进行的体内空间转录组学分析显示，心脏、肝脏和肠道中的细胞组成向年轻动物状态转变，同时上调了调控解毒、线粒体稳定性、能量代谢及抗氧化作用的基因。一项基于人类蛋白质组学分析的5000重随机试验显示，唑来膦酸治疗后约400种蛋白质发生显著变化，其中与基因组不稳定性、蛋白质稳态丧失、线粒体功能障碍、干细胞耗竭及衰老相关分泌表型（SASP）相关的蛋白质下调。荧光标记及追踪证实了双膦酸盐被非骨骼细胞摄取。此外，多种临床常用双膦酸盐在低剂量下可刺激多种人类细胞类型的生长，并保护其免受DNA损伤诱导的衰老，其中对心肌细胞的作用最为显著。最后，利用AlphaFold进行的全蛋白质组靶点去卷积识别出先前未知的结合伙伴，包括PHB2和ASAH1，并验证了MEF2A的下游上调是唑来膦酸在心肌细胞中触发益处的关键介质。综合来看，这些结果确定了BP在多种非骨骼组织中潜在的促长寿（geroprotective）机制。
